_readme: Edit this file to change the deck. Add, remove or rewrite freely. Fields: d = domain (friendships | dating | reading | housework), s = suit, t = title, b = the card body, q = the question you get asked when you play it, xp = points. The q field is what the chronicler builds the chapter from, so make it ask for something physical and specific.

cards.b: Message someone with no agenda attached. Not a plan, not a favour. Just contact.
cards.q: Who, and what did you send?

cards.b: Not we should catch up. A day, a place, a time, sent to one person.
cards.q: What did you propose, and what came back?

cards.b: When someone answers, ask the one underneath it. Stay for the answer.
cards.q: What was the question underneath?

cards.b: Tell someone plainly what you value in them. No hedging, no joke at the end.
cards.q: What did you tell them? Their words back, if you have them.

cards.b: Once today, do not rush to fill a pause. See what arrives in it.
cards.q: What arrived in the pause?

cards.b: Walk in as the person you would like to be, before you feel like her.
cards.q: Who did you walk in as?

cards.b: After seeing someone, send the thing you said you would send.
cards.q: What did you send, and how long had you been meaning to?

cards.b: Do the thing you would do alone anyway, and leave the door open.
cards.q: What did you do, and who came?

cards.b: Ask someone out, plainly, without softening it into something deniable.
cards.q: What did you say? Word for word, if you remember.

cards.b: Say the true thing you would normally file down before letting it out.
cards.q: What was the sentence, before you would have filed it?

cards.b: Get turned down, and log it here. This pays more than a smooth yes. That is the point.
cards.q: How did it land? Not how you think it should have landed.

cards.b: Message first. Say something only you would say.
cards.q: What did you open with?

cards.b: Hold eye contact past the point where you would usually look away.
cards.q: What happened in the extra second?

cards.b: Write down, for yourself only, what you are actually looking for this year.
cards.q: What did you write down?

cards.b: If it is not right, end it kindly and go home. Leaving well is a skill.
cards.q: How did you end it, and what was the walk home like?

cards.b: Copy out a sentence worth keeping. By hand, if you can.
cards.q: What caught you about it?

cards.b: Explain what you are reading to a person who is not reading it.
cards.q: Who, and where did you get stuck explaining it?

cards.b: Read something written before you were born. Anything.
cards.q: What was it, and what felt foreign?

cards.b: Return to the book you left at page sixty. Give it thirty more.
cards.q: Why did you leave it the first time?

cards.b: Find the thing you disagree with and write the objection down.
cards.q: What is your objection?

cards.b: Paper only. Phone in another room. Timer if you need one.
cards.q: Where were you, and what did you notice?

cards.b: Chase one reference out of one book and into another.
cards.q: Where did it take you?

cards.b: Write down what you remember before you look. The looking is not the learning.
cards.q: What could you not remember?

cards.b: Do the review that is due, not the new material that is tempting.
cards.q: What had gone, that you thought was solid?

cards.t: The one you keep getting wrong
cards.b: Find the error you repeat. Drill only that, ten minutes, nothing else.
cards.q: What is the error, and what does it cost you?

cards.b: Use the language with a person today. Mistakes included, mistakes expected.
cards.q: What did you fail to say?

cards.b: Go through one room naming everything in the other language. Look up what you cannot say.
cards.q: Which thing had no name?

cards.b: Explain a rule you half-know, out loud. Notice exactly where you stall.
cards.q: Where exactly did you stall?

cards.b: Fifteen minutes of study right before bed. Check it in the morning before anything else.
cards.q: What survived the night?

cards.b: Say them in a sentence you invented, not the one the book gave you.
cards.q: Which word would not stay?

cards.b: The one you have been avoiding. You know which.
cards.q: What was in it?

cards.b: Every flat surface empty before you sleep.
cards.q: What was the last thing you put away?

cards.b: Whatever is worst. Ten minutes only. Stop when it rings.
cards.q: What did you choose, and did you stop?

cards.b: Given away, binned, or returned. It does not sleep here tonight.
cards.q: What went, and how long had it been here?

cards.b: Sheets, towels, the lot. Sleep in it afterwards.
cards.q: What did the bed feel like?

cards.b: All of them. Turn the ones reaching for the window.
cards.q: Which one is struggling?

cards.b: Not clean. Beautiful. There is a difference and you know it.
cards.q: Which corner, and what did you do to it?
